summary.headline: NMDC guides FY27 production to 60 million tonnes and FY27 capex to about INR6,000 crore, with Q1 FY27 output up about 15% YoY.
summary.overview: NMDC reported FY26 production above 50 million tonnes and an 11% PAT rise despite sluggish prices, with management citing a record capex of about INR3,300 crore. Management guided FY27 production to 60 million tonnes, with the first two months of Q1 FY27 about 15% higher YoY at roughly 10 million tonnes. New iron ore (Deposit 4, Deposit 13) and coal (Tokisud, Rohne) assets are being commissioned, and a INR3,000 crore blending yard at Vizag is sanctioned. The EBITDA margin was 33% group-level, down from 42%, due to a one-time HR coil trading arrangement with NMDC Steel; standalone iron ore EBITDA was stated at 42%.

segments.name: Iron ore (NMDC standalone)
segments.commentary: Standalone EBITDA margin at 42%, with FY27 guided at 42-43%. Kirandul FY26 about 21 million tonnes (to ~30 million by decade-end); Bacheli about 18-19 million tonnes (to ~35 million).

segments.name: NMDC Steel (NSL)
segments.commentary: NSL has turned profitable; the HR coil trading in the last quarter was a one-time cash-flow support and is not expected in Q1 FY27. NSL dues are being recovered at about INR100 crore per month, with full liquidation in 16-18 months (pre-demerger dues about INR2,500 crore, now about INR1,800 crore).

segments.name: Coal
segments.commentary: Tokisud (2.3 million tonnes peak, thermal, opened) targets 0.75-1 million tonnes in FY27 from Q2; Rohne (8 million tonnes peak coking coal) opens around end-Q3 FY27 with no FY27 production. Management expects INR500-600 crore revenue per 1 million tonnes at G10 grade, at 30-40% EBITDA (approximate).

segments.name: Pellets (KIOCL)
segments.commentary: KIOCL 3 million tonne job-work plant: FY26 about 2.4 million tonnes; FY27 target 3-3.3 million tonnes. Pellet grade achieved 66.5% Fe; targeting 67% DR-grade with a $20-30/t premium.

guidance_outlook: FY27 production guided at 60 million tonnes including NSL, built from Deposit 14 (+1 mt), NMZ (+1 mt), Kumaraswamy (+~3.3 mt), Deposit 5 (+2 mt to 12 mt), plus Deposit 4 (~1 mt) and Deposit 13 (~0.5 mt).
Deposit 4 expected to start commercial mining in Q2 FY27: about 1 mt in FY27, 2 mt in FY28, and 7 mt peak rated capacity after 1.5-2 more years.
Deposit 13 start targeted around Q2 FY27 after pending clearances: under 0.5 mt in FY27, about 2 mt next year, 10 mt initial peak rising to 20-21 mt in 4-5 years.
Capex guidance: about INR6,000 crore in FY27 (range INR6,000-7,000 crore); INR7,000-10,000 crore per year over the next 2-3 years; INR40,000-50,000 crore over 3 years to reach 100 mt.
Overseas critical mineral and mineral asset acquisitions: INR2,000-3,000 crore expected in FY27; a couple of overseas assets targeted this year.
Management reiterated a 100 million tonne target by end of decade and said the 60 mt FY27 guidance is achievable without the railway doubling, but 100 mt requires it.
No immediate plans to leverage the balance sheet; internal accruals expected to fund capex and acquisitions, with debt possible late FY27 only for large global acquisitions.
Iron ore prices expected to stay range-bound in FY27; monthly price calls to be taken.
capex_capacity: Railway: 131 km doubling; two sections remaining, one by end of June 2026 and the Bhansi-Bacheli section by December 2026; evacuation capacity to rise from 28-30 mt to ~40 mt, with 60 mt+ after doubling beyond Jagdalpur.
Slurry pipeline (15 mt, Bacheli to Nagarnar), Nagarnar pellet plant and Bacheli grinding mill in pre-commissioning; commissioning expected by end-June or mid-July 2026.
EC capacity 64.8 mt vs CTO ~55.4 mt; CTO enhancement sought in three places to ~58.8 mt. All mines reached EC capacity as of 1 April 2026 (Deposit 5 the exception in FY26).
Deposit 5 downhill conveyor and bottleneck fix due June-July 2026, enabling 12 mt. New infrastructure at Deposit 14, NMZ, 11 and 11C takes about 1.5 years, adding 5-6 mt.
INR3,000 crore blending yard at Vizag (board sanctioned, ~2-2.5 year build); Vizag land parcel ~1,100 acres; pellet plant at Vizag on drawing board, pending slurry pipeline route decision.
Expansion works (~INR15,000-20,000 crore worth of major tenders) expected to be awarded by end-June or July 2026.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is not a constraint even at 100 mt, citing JSW, AMNS (10 mt plant near Vizag, 17 mt total), JSPL and NSL expansions; NMDC's phosphorus content of 0.05% is a claimed differentiator.

Iron ore prices expected range-bound in Q1 FY27 after steel prices peaked Dec-Feb and stabilised in March-April; the company sets prices monthly, citing international prices, competitor prices and logistics, not a direct steel-price link.
RINL consumes 7-8 mt per year; bills discounted at ~10% premium with a 45-day payment lag; no recourse to NMDC in FY25 or FY26.
Blended/branded iron ore (Vizag) planned as a premium product; exports unattractive given 30% export duty, so pellets are preferred for export.
Iron ore realisation slightly down ~2% per an analyst question; no quantified FY27 realisation guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Mine-wise bridge to 60 mt FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Deposit 14 +1 mt, NMZ +1 mt, Kumaraswamy +~3.3 mt (MPAP relief from 8.6 mt), Deposit 5 +2 mt (to 12 mt), totalling ~5.3 mt; plus Deposit 4 (~1 mt) and Deposit 13 (~0.5 mt) gives ~60 mt including NSL.

qa_highlights.question: Coal mine economics and grade?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial volume mostly via auction at prices above CIL FSA; 1 mt is estimated at INR500-600 crore revenue with 30-40% EBITDA. Grade is G10; figures described as very preliminary.

qa_highlights.question: Recovery of NSL and RINL receivables?
qa_highlights.answer: NSL dues cut from ~INR2,500 crore to ~INR1,800 crore; recovery at ~INR100 crore per month, 16-18 months for NSL, about a year and a half to two for the rest. RINL is 100% government-owned, with timing slower but no risk assumed.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans and critical minerals spending?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex ~INR6,000 crore (range 6,000-7,000), then INR7,000-10,000 crore per year. Overseas acquisitions INR2,000-3,000 crore in FY27; domestic rare earth via GMDC MoU in Gujarat, no firm profitability guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Can 60 mt be reached without railway doubling?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, 60 mt is achievable without it, but 100 mt is not possible without the doubling completing (Vizag/Bhansi-Bacheli section due December 2026).

qa_highlights.question: Deposit 4, Deposit 13 and Rohne ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Deposit 4 ~1 mt in FY27, 2 mt in FY28, 7 mt peak; Deposit 13 under 0.5 mt FY27, 2 mt next year, 10 mt initially rising to 20-21 mt; Rohne opens around end-Q3 FY27 with no FY27 output and 8 mt peak coking coal.

qa_highlights.question: EBITDA guidance and realisation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Iron ore EBITDA margin to be maintained at 42-43% for FY27; no specific per-tonne realisation or EBITDA-per-tonne figures were given.

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 output and CTO enhancement to ~58.8 mt (vs EC 64.8 mt) are needed to hit 60 mt; EC and forest clearances remain a continuous process.
Railway doubling completion (December 2026 for Bhansi-Bacheli) is a prerequisite for 100 mt.
NSL and RINL receivables recovery pace and any repeat of HR coil trading; the one-time trading hit margins in Q4 FY26.
Pending approvals for Deposit 13 and Rohne coal; Rohne has no FY27 output.
Govt pay revision: provisions already taken from 1 January 2026; further provisioning for executives from 1 January 2027.
Overseas acquisition pipeline and the decision to use debt for large global deals late FY27.

financial_highlights.value: above 50 million tonnes (about 53 million tonnes per CMD)

financial_highlights.change: Down from 42%, due to steel trading
About 15% higher YoY vs 8.2 million tonnes

key_quotes: We have touched 53 million tons of production, we have crossed that.
We'll not be able to do 100 without this, but 60 we can.
I don't expect a sharp increase, they would be rather range-bound.
So it will be very difficult to give you a guidance about how profitable it is, but we are, we know that rare earth and other critical minerals are the future
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on volumes, capex and the 100 mt ambition, citing CTO/EC headroom and Q1 FY27 run-rate. Noticeably cautious or evasive on realisation (prices "range-bound", no per-tonne guidance), on critical-mineral acquisition capex and profitability ("very speculative"), and on RINL receivables recovery timing.
